member.name: T:Microsoft.VisualBasic.MIME.application.json.JSONLogic.jsonLogic
member.summary: Build complex rules, serialize them as JSON, share them between front-end and back-end
member.remarks:
If you’re looking for a way to share logic between front-end and back-end code, and even store it in a database, JsonLogic might be a fit for you.
JsonLogic isn't a full programming language. It’s a small, safe way to delegate one decision. You could store a rule in a database to decide later. You could send that rule from back-end to front-end so the decision is made immediately from user input. Because the rule is data, you can even build it dynamically from user actions or GUI input.
JsonLogic has no setters, no loops, no functions Or gotos. One rule leads To one decision, With no side effects And deterministic computation time.
> https://jsonlogic.com/

member.name: T:Microsoft.VisualBasic.MIME.application.json.LenientJson.LenientJsonParser
member.summary: A lenient (fault-tolerant) JSON parser designed to automatically repair and parse JSON output produced by Large Language Models (LLMs).

remarks.para: This parser implements a "Lenient Recursive Descent Parser" strategy inspired by the json-repair library. Instead of parsing first and then repairing, it tolerates errors during the parsing process itself by scanning the input character-by-character with a cursor.
The following 16 repair strategies are implemented:

item.description: Skip comments (// line and /* block */ comments)
Ignore extra content after the first JSON value
Accept unescaped control characters in strings

Smart quote closure detection — when a quote is encountered inside a string, lookahead to check if the next non-whitespace character is a structural character (, } ] : or EOF) before treating it as the closing quote; otherwise keep it as an internal unescaped quote
Missing closing quote recovery — repair a value string whose closing quote was dropped, causing it to swallow the ", " separator and the following key name

remarks.para: Strategy 16 in detail. A very common LLM failure is to omit the closing quote of a string value, for example emitting {"module_name": "demo,goal": "the goal text"} instead of the correct {"module_name": "demo", "goal": "the goal text"} Without special handling this is catastrophic rather than local: the value is read as demo,goal, the stray : is skipped, and the following text is consumed as the next key. Every subsequent key and value is shifted by one, so the whole document degenerates into garbage keys and no usable content survives.

The repair keys off a hard guarantee of the JSON grammar rather than a heuristic: a string in value position may only be followed by ,, }, ] or EOF — never by :. So a colon there is proof that the closing quote was dropped. The parser then splits the string at its last comma: the text before it is the true value, the text after it is the swallowed key. The last comma is used because real values often contain commas (prose, file paths, CJK text) whereas the swallowed key is an identifier that virtually never does. Because valid JSON can never trigger the condition, well-formed documents are unaffected. If the string contains no comma the parser degrades to the previous behaviour, so the strategy can only ever improve the result.

member.name: M:Microsoft.VisualBasic.MIME.application.json.LenientJson.LenientJsonParser.parse_object
member.summary: Parse a JSON object { "key": value, ... }. Implements: - Strategy 6: Auto-close unclosed objects at EOF (truncation repair) - Strategy 7: Skip trailing commas - Strategy 8: Tolerate missing colons - Strategy 9: Accept unquoted keys - Strategy 16: Missing closing quote recovery — split a value string that swallowed the separator and the following key back into its two parts

member.name: M:Microsoft.VisualBasic.MIME.application.json.LenientJson.LenientJsonParser.is_likely_closing_quote(Microsoft.VisualBasic.MIME.application.json.LenientJson.LenientJsonParser.StringContext,System.Boolean@)
member.summary: Determine whether the quote character just consumed at m_index - 1 is likely the real closing quote of a string.
member.para: When the parser encounters a quote character inside a string, it does not immediately treat it as the closing quote. Instead, it looks ahead past any whitespace to find the next non-whitespace character:

item.description: If the next non-whitespace character is one of ,, }, ], :, or EOF, this quote is treated as the real closing quote (these are the only legal characters that can follow a string value in valid JSON).
Otherwise (the next character is a letter, digit, or any other non-structural character), this quote is treated as an internal unescaped quote and is kept in the string content.

member.para: This handles the common LLM error of embedding unescaped quotes inside string values, e.g.:

example.code: "evidence": "Multiple papers: "HIF-1 induces GLUT1" and "PDK1" in cells."

member.para: Strategy 16 refines this test with syntactic context. A : is a legal successor only when the string sits in the key position. In the value position JSON permits only ,, }, ] or EOF, so a : there is proof that the value's closing quote was omitted. The quote is still accepted as the terminator (the string has to end somewhere), but is raised so the caller can split the swallowed key back out.
member.param: The syntactic position of the string being parsed.
Receives True when the terminator was accepted in the position but is followed by :, i.e. the missing-closing-quote error of Strategy 16.
member.returns: True if the quote is likely the real closing quote; False if it is likely an internal unescaped quote.
